dedupe_keys.name: esa worldcover 10 m global land cover

description: ESA WorldCover provides the first global land cover maps for 2020 and 2021 at 10 m resolution, developed and validated in near-real time from Sentinel-1 radar and Sentinel-2 optical data by a consortium led by VITO for the European Space Agency's Earth Observation Envelope Programme. Each map has eleven classes, including tree cover, shrubland, grassland, cropland, built-up, bare and sparse vegetation, snow and ice, permanent water bodies, herbaceous wetland, mangroves and moss and lichen, and comes with a user manual and a validation report. The 2021 version 200 is cited as Zanaga et al. (2022), doi:10.5281/zenodo.7254221. Data are available from the WorldCover viewer and downloads, from Zenodo and in the Google Earth Engine catalogue as ESA/WorldCover/v200, under the CC BY 4.0 licence at no cost. Caveats: only two epochs exist, version 100 (2020) and version 200 (2021) used different algorithms so change between them is not reliable, and class accuracy varies by region. It is used to map green and blue infrastructure, vegetation and wetlands near infrastructure corridors, roughness and land use for flood and heat hazard exposure models, and climate adaptation studies; related records are the JRC Global Surface Water dataset and the Copernicus Urban Atlas.
